svg.text: Read every upper-limb X-ray the same way
1 · Skeletal maturity: physis (growth plate) visible and unfused = immature · fused = mature
2 · Bone: cortex, medulla, density, generalized bone disease
5 · Soft tissues: abnormal even when the bones look normal
Bone pathology, TIMS-C: Trauma, tumours · Infection, inflammatory, idiopathic · Metabolic, malignancy · Systemic, senile
STANDARD SERIES (trauma, osteoarthritis): AP · Y-view · Grashey
No Grashey image in this year's module. It also reads the axillary view.

• Sublime tubercle = ulnar collateral ligament attachment
• Ulna: olecranon, trochlear notch, coronoid: all fracture-prone
CHECK ON THE LATERAL: fat pads + two lines (normal films)
• Posterior fat pad: not normally seen

• Along the radial shaft → centre of the capitellum

FINDINGS: SOFT TISSUES (osteoarthritis: see the last band)
• Well-defined, low-density oval mass = lipoma (confirmed on CT or MRI)
• Always look at the soft tissues
STANDARD VIEWS: AP · lateral, then the arcs of Gilula on the AP
• Distal row: trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate
• Distal radioulnar joint, radial + ulnar styloids
• Lister's tubercle (dorsal radius): check it for fracture
• Carpals overlap, so the AP is essential for
1 · Proximal surfaces of the proximal row
2 · Distal surfaces of the proximal row
3 · Proximal surfaces of the distal row
• Break, step-off or widening → carpal injury
FINDINGS: check every bone, since a fracture can keep the arcs intact
• Lucent line through the scaphoid's proximal
• Expanded distal radius, large lytic lesion
ANY JOINT = 3 FINDINGS, graded mild, moderate or severe on the combination
• Narrowing, sclerosis and osteophytes at the glenohumeral
